source_text: I. Decius imperator volens opprimere vel superare legem Christianorum, decreta constituit per universum orbem ut omnes Christiani recedentes a deo vivo et vero daemoniis sacrificarent, qui vero noluissent, suppliciis subiacerent. eo tempore famulus dei Maximus, vir sanctus, ultro se palam ostendit. erat vero plebeius, negotii sui curam gerens. comprehensus igitur oblatus est Optimo proconsuli apud Asiam. proconsul dixit ad eum: Quis vocaris? respondit: Maximus dicor. proconsul dixit: Cuius condicionis es? Maximus dixit: Ingenuus natus, servus vero Christi. proconsul dixit: Quod officium geris? Maximus respondit: Homo sum plebeius, meo negotio vivens. proconsul dixit: Christianus es? Maximus respondit: Etsi peccator, Christianus tamen sum. proconsul dixit: Non cognovisti decreta invictissimorum principum quae nuper advenerunt? Maximus respondit: Quae? proconsul dixit: Ut omnes Christiani relicta superflua superstitione cognoscant verum principem, cui omnia subiacent, et eius deos adorent. Maximus respondit: Iniquam regis huius saeculi prolatam sententiam cognovi, et ideo me palam ostendi. proconsul dixit: Sacrifica ergo diis. Maximus respondit: Ego non sacrifico nisi soli deo, cui me ab ineunte aetate sacrificasse congratulor. proconsul dixit: Sacrifica ut salveris; quod si nolueris, variis faciam te deficere tormentis. Maximus respondit: Hoc est quod semper optavi. propterea enim me manifestavi, ut tandem carens miserabili et temporali vita aeternam reciperem.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: Decius as emperor wanting to crush and overcome the law of the Christians set up decrees through the whole world, that all Christians withdrawing from the living and true God should sacrifice to demons, and those unwilling should undergo punishments; at that time Maximus the servant of God, a holy man, willingly showed himself openly; he was a plebeian managing his own business; arrested he was brought to Optimus the proconsul in Asia; interrogation follows about name, status, occupation, Christian identity, knowledge of the princes' decrees, order to know the true prince and worship his gods, refusal, order to sacrifice to the gods, claim to sacrifice only to the one God since earliest age, threat of various torments unless he sacrifices for his safety, and answer that this was always desired, for therefore he revealed himself that finally losing wretched temporal life he might receive eternal life.
pass_b_english: The emperor Decius, wishing to crush and overthrow the law of the Christians, established decrees throughout the whole world, that all Christians, falling away from the living and true God, should sacrifice to demons, and that those who refused should be subjected to punishments.
At that time Maximus, a servant of God and a holy man, willingly showed himself in public.
He was a commoner, looking after his own business.
He was therefore arrested and brought before Optimus, the proconsul in Asia.
The proconsul said to him, What are you called?
He answered, I am called Maximus.
The proconsul said, What is your condition?
Maximus said, Born free, but a slave of Christ.
The proconsul said, What work do you do?
Maximus answered, I am an ordinary man, living by my own trade.
The proconsul said, Are you a Christian?
Maximus answered, Though a sinner, yet I am a Christian.
The proconsul said, Have you not learned of the decrees of the most unconquered princes which recently arrived?
Maximus answered, What decrees?
The proconsul said, That all Christians, abandoning their idle superstition, should acknowledge the true prince, to whom all things are subject, and should worship his gods.
Maximus answered, I have learned of the unjust sentence put forth by this king of the world, and for that reason I showed myself openly.
The proconsul said, Sacrifice therefore to the gods.
Maximus answered, I sacrifice to no one except to God alone, and I rejoice that I have offered myself to him from my earliest age.
The proconsul said, Sacrifice so that you may be saved; but if you refuse, I will make you fail under varied tortures.
Maximus answered, This is what I have always desired.
For I revealed myself for this very reason, that at last, rid of this wretched and temporal life, I might receive eternal life.

choices.why: vero is adversative here, contrasting earthly free birth with spiritual bondage to Christ, so it requires but rather than and.
ablative meo negotio gives means of livelihood, and vivens is making a living, not merely being alive.

choices.english: I will make you fail under varied tortures
choices.why: faciam with infinitive deficere is causative, and variis tormentis is instrumental ablative, so the torments are the means of wearing him out.
rejected: I will fail you with torments
